items.author: strategist
items.text: The Highland Valley Copper strike ends with a ratified new labour agreement

evidence.note: A CBC headline reports Highland Valley Copper was ordered to stop using replacement workers, which pressures the company toward a deal, but no tentative or ratified agreement appears in today's news, and the headline gives no figures.

Today's HR Law Canada item (news 15) says Teck is barred from using newly promoted supervisors during the B.C. copper strike, which adds pressure toward a deal, but no tentative or ratified agreement appears and the headline gives no figures.
Items 135 (over 1,000 workers in two B.C. strikes) and the HR Law item on Teck's barred use of newly promoted supervisors add pressure toward a deal, but no tentative or ratified agreement appears.

items.author: geologist
items.text: The Highland Valley Copper strike ends, with a tentative or ratified labour agreement announced by the company or the union

evidence.note: The same CBC headline (Highland Valley Copper ordered to stop using replacement workers) bears on a tentative or ratified agreement without showing one yet, and it gives no figures.
The same HR Law Canada item (news 15) shows added pressure on Highland Valley Copper to settle, but neither a tentative nor a ratified agreement is reported, and the headline gives no figures.
Item 135 (over 1,000 workers in two B.C. strikes) and the Teck supervisor restriction show pressure to settle, but neither a tentative nor a ratified agreement is reported.

items.author: strategist
items.text: The American Samoa deep-sea mineral lease sale is postponed or halted, by court order or government action, before 2026-12-31
items.verdict_note: The American Samoa sale went ahead, with the leases sold to one bidder for about $6 million (items 66, 90, 96), and despite the court setback it was not postponed or halted (items 113, 132).

items.text: Spot gold trades above US$4,000 per ounce on at least one day

evidence.note: Gold has fallen below $3,600 and hit a 14-month low (items 110, 129), so a move above $4,000 by June 2027 would need a rise of more than 10%, and today's news points against it.
